Coleman is the top claim on this wire, and the depth chart is the reason. He was a strong prospect coming out of college, big enough to stay on the field on every down, and it was a surprise when he lasted until the fourth round of the NFL draft. The problem for fantasy was never the talent, it was that he opened the season as the third back in Denver behind JK Dobbins and RJ Harvey. Then Harvey hurt his hamstring in practice and missed Week 2, and Dobbins hurt his own hamstring in the same game Coleman scored in.
The reporting on Monday, September 21 had neither injury as serious, and there is a real chance both are back for the Rams in Week 3. If they are, Coleman goes back to being the third back. If one of them sits, he gets a game to prove he is the most talented back in that building, and if both sit he is a top 20 running back on my board for the week. That range is worth a claim in every league.

Boston was either drafted in your league or picked up after his Week 1 touchdown, and he has now scored in both games while staying on the field for nearly every Cleveland snap. With Jerry Jeudy a non factor, the WR1 job in that offense is wide open, and the Browns looked better against Tampa Bay than anyone expected, well enough that the betting markets give them a real chance at home against Carolina in Week 3.
I still do not expect Cleveland to win many games, and in a 10 team league with 2 receivers and 1 flex he does not move the needle. In a 12 team league with 2 flex spots he is a flex play sooner rather than later, and if that offense is a little better than we projected, an every down receiver in it starts to matter.

Bigsby is the other name at the top of this wire, and the honest version is that his week depends on news that had not arrived yet. Barkley finished Week 2, and through Monday, September 21 there had been no update on his injury. If Barkley is cleared, Bigsby is a handcuff you hold. If he is not, Bigsby gets the majority of the touches at Chicago.
Temper the ceiling either way. With Barkley off the field in Week 2, Philadelphia telegraphed the play call: Will Shipley on the field meant a dropback, Bigsby on the field meant a run. That is a committee, not a workhorse, so Bigsby is not the top 12 back a Barkley injury would suggest. He is also very likely rostered already.

Gadsden was the biggest loser of training camp, because every report out of Los Angeles said the Chargers wanted their tight ends to block and he is the receiving type. David Njoku played ahead of him, Charlie Kolar was paid to block, and Gadsden saw 18% of the snaps in Week 1.
Now Njoku and Kolar are both on injured reserve, and a tight end who barely played in Week 1 projects to play 70 to 80% of the snaps from Week 3 on. He is a hold rather than a start until we see it, and I would not empty the budget for him, but tight end is thin enough that the man about to run most of the routes in an NFL offense is worth a roster spot.

Mitchell was not interesting after Week 1. Then Omar Cooper Jr., the first round pick the Jets drafted to start opposite Garrett Wilson, went to injured reserve, and Mitchell stepped into an every down role with the kind of target volume you start in a 12 team league.
I do not think he is especially talented, and a Jets receiver is normally a hard pass, but the Jets have moved the ball well through 2 games, and with Kenyon Sadiq starting slow there is nobody else to throw to. He is a flex play until Cooper is back, not a piece you build around.

DEEPER LEAGUES
Alvin Kamara  RB · NO
Week 2 at BAL: 9 carries · 15 rushing yards · 6 targets · 7.2 PPR
Back on the radar as the premium handcuff behind Travis Etienne after Kellen Moore built him into the passing game in Week 2. He does not have that juice anymore and I would not start him unless Etienne goes down, but if that happens the receiving work alone makes him a top 24 back in full PPR.
Emanuel Wilson  RB · SEA
Week 2 at ARI: 21 carries · 92 rushing yards · 1 target · 9.2 PPR
Only matters if Jadarian Price misses Week 3 with the shoulder injury, and the reporting on Monday, September 21 had Price more likely than not to play. If Price sits, Wilson is startable, because Seattle is about a touchdown favorite at Washington and should be running the ball in the second half.
Terrance Ferguson  TE · LAR
Week 2 vs NYG: 9 targets · 6 receptions · 54 yards · 17.4 PPR
Looked like the Rams starting tight end in Week 2 with Puka Nacua out, and a second round pick in his second season who flashed at the end of his rookie year is worth a look in deeper leagues. He is far better with no Nacua on the field, so treat him as a 1 week play unless Nacua misses again.
Dontayvion Wicks  WR · PHI
Week 2 at TEN: 6 targets · 5 receptions · 74 yards · 12.4 PPR
Dallas Goedert is out for the next few weeks in Philadelphia and Wicks saw more work in Week 2 than he did in Week 1. He could be a viable bye week fill in for deeper leagues.
DON’T CHASE
Rashod Bateman  WR · BAL
Week 2 vs NO: 9 targets · 7 receptions · 88 yards · 21.8 PPR
If you picked him up and started him in Week 2, incredible. But Zay Flowers should be back in Week 3, and with Flowers on the field Bateman is not usable.
Jameis Winston  QB · NYG
Week 2 at LAR: 111 passing yards · 0 passing TDs · 1 rushing yard · 2.5 PPR
Do not replace Jaxson Dart with his backup unless you are in a superflex league. Winston looked like he should not be seeing the field, and the Giants offense with him under center is over.
Marcus Mariota  QB · WAS
Week 2 at DAL: 111 passing yards · 1 passing TD · 3 rushing yards · 8.7 PPR
The same rule applies in Washington, where Mariota is the confirmed Week 3 starter with nobody expecting Jayden Daniels back soon, and he is still not the answer in a 1 quarterback league.
QUARTERBACK STREAMERS
Jordan Love  QB · GB
Week 2 at NYJ: 145 passing yards · 2 passing TDs · 0 rushing yards · 13.8 PPR
The streamer I like most for Week 3, and I may start him over Drake Maye myself. Green Bay is about a touchdown favorite over Atlanta, projects as one of the highest scoring offenses on the slate, and cannot run the ball, so the volume goes through Love against maybe the worst defense in the league. A 1 week play, not a rest of season answer.
Kyler Murray  QB · MIN
Week 2: did not play
Cleared concussion protocol and named the Week 3 starter, and he gets a Tampa Bay defense that just lost to Cleveland. The rushing floor is what separates him from the other streamers, and Minnesota projects as a middle of the road offense, so he is the one with real rest of season upside if you lost Daniels or Caleb Williams.
Tyler Shough  QB · NO
Week 2 at BAL: 252 passing yards · 1 passing TD · 23 rushing yards · 22.4 PPR
Week 1 had the overtime inflation, but Week 2 against Baltimore was a matchup I expected the Saints to lose badly, and Shough played well and ran a little too. Worth the roster spot if you lost your starter, and he is here to stay.
DEFENSES TO STREAM
My pick: Vikings at Buccaneers
Tampa Bay just lost to Cleveland, which is not an offense to fear, and the Vikings get the Dolphins the week after, so this is a pickup that gives you 2 usable weeks. It is a talented defense that just held Chicago to 3 points, and it is the one I am going after myself.
Also in play
Giants vs Titans · Panthers at Browns · Packers vs Falcons · Bengals at Steelers
How I pick them
I stream defenses off the betting markets: the biggest spread on the slate and the lowest projected total for the other offense. The best plays in Week 3 are Seattle at Washington and Kansas City against Miami, and both are probably rostered in your league already, which is why the list starts where it does.
